k:HH.Finance.Lottery.News.Colony: Your lottery drew {0}: {1} jackpot winners among {2} tickets.
k:HH.Finance.Lottery.ColonyIntro: Guests and the simulated players of friendly settlements buy tickets. Four numbers out of 25. You keep what is not paid out, the pot only pays what it holds.
k:HH.Finance.Lottery.Demand: Your draw: {0} % back, global: {1} % → about {2} tickets a day ({3} from guests, {4} from far away).
k:HH.Finance.Lottery.PotModel: Pot model: no risk. Prizes come out of the pot, nothing else.
k:HH.Finance.Help.Line: Gambling for real? If it stops being fun, real help is here:
k:HH.Finance.Help.Tip: Opens the website in your browser.
A savings account. The money lies in a very secure mattress and grows a little. In a bank run withdrawals are locked for two days.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_Outlander: Loans to a union of outlander towns that is building roads, wells and one disputed bridge. Pays on time, until it does not. After a default you get roughly a third back.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_EmpireWar: Bonds that finance a war of the Empire. When the war ends in victory they jump, in defeat they are worth a nice frame. The war has been going on for a long time, mostly in the brochures.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_Index.des: The fifty biggest companies of the rim in one product. The reference for everything else on this page: the profitability slider is defined by what this one earns on average.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_StockMica: Shares of a league of outlander towns. Quarterly numbers move the price; so do your relations with the league, a little. It pays no dividend but sends a lovely calendar.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_StockTrib: Shares of a tribal cooperative that sells hides, hearth wood and an astonishing amount of hospitality. Highly dependent on the weather and on the mood of one very large uncle.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_StockEmpi: The company behind the imperial ceremonies: banners, trumpets and tiny crowns. Profits depend on how many nobles feel offended by how little.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_StockColo: A holding that owns exactly one thing: the idea that your colony is a destination. Reacts to your wealth and to raids you survive. You have a stake in its success, but so does everybody who read this.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_GrowthFun: An actively managed fund. The managers have a very impressive brochure and a boat. Their skill is, on average, slightly negative, and it was fixed when the fund was founded.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_PietyBond: Bonds backed by the donations of seventeen faiths, each convinced the other sixteen are doing it wrong. Steady, solemn, and very slightly smug.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_RelicFutu: Futures on relics that may or may not exist, to be delivered by a courier who may or may not be a prophet. The contract was blessed.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_RimCoin.d: A digital coin that is entirely made of electricity and conviction. Swings several percent a day, makes jumps nobody can explain and sits on an exchange that has been hacked before. And will be.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_MemeThrum: A coin named after a rare beast and backed by exactly as much. The whitepaper is a drawing of a thrumbo. The founder is, according to the drawing, a thrumbo.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_MemeBooma: A coin that explodes in value. And occasionally just explodes. Popular among people who like the smell of burning money.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_MemeMuffa: The community coin of everybody who loves muffalo and nothing else. Its roadmap is a picture of a muffalo looking at the moon. The roadmap has not changed.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_NftThrumb: A collection of pictures of thrumbos, each unique, each a little bit like the others. You own a receipt for a picture of a picture. Buyers appear slowly and want a discount.
d:Silverline.AssetDef/SL_Asset_NftMuffal: Certificate of Ownership: Picture of a Muffalo
An ownership certificate of a picture of a muffalo. The picture is stored somewhere. The certificate is stored in your account. Neither of them smells of muffalo.
